newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani stocks seen up 25 percent - report.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani stocks seen up 25 percent - report.

text.p: The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index is likely to rise at least 25 percent in the next six months on an improved economic and political outlook, a research report of Crosby Securities said.
"We are optimistic about the KSE's performance in 1997, expecting it to rise at least 25 percent in the next six months," said the December report, released on Tuesday.
It said investor interest was expected to revive from mid-January following indicators showing a stronger economy and in anticipation of a stable, democratically elected government.
President Farooq Leghari promised to hold fresh elections on February 3 when he dismissed the government of Benazir Bhutto on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.

Crosby Securities, an affiliate of stockbrokers Societe General, said the outlook on external accounts was still relatively unfavourable but liquid foreign reserves were expected to increase to $1.0 billion by mid-January.

Reserves would be boosted by disbursement of at least $160 million from a stalled International Monetary Fund standby loan and about $500 million in dollar-for-rupee swap funds that banks and financial institutions are expected to bring in, it said.

Crosby said the caretaker government was expected to launch much-needed financial sector reforms by mid-December along with cuts in development and non-development expenditures aimed at reducing the fiscal deficit to four percent of gross domestic product from 6.3 percent in 1995/96 (July-June).
The government was also expected to reduce its local bank borrowing to 52 billion rupees from 66 billion by the end of December by tapping short-term foreign commercial borrowing.

Crosby said this would help release domestic resources to the private sector, but added a word of caution, saying the Pakistani market, with its weak retail base, depended heavily on funds pumped in by foreign and local institutions.
Crosby predicted that the Karachi 100-index, which closed at 1,462.54 points on Monday, would hit 2,040 points next year but advised investors to exit at around 1,900.

In the absence of much international interest in investment in Pakistan in the short term, any major market movements above the 1,900-point level would trigger net selling by small investors, the report said.

"However, we do expect some reallocation of regional portfolios away from the Bangladesh market, which has experienced an increase of over 250 percent during the past year, towards Pakistan and Sri Lanka," it added.
The sluggish performance of the Pakistani and Sri Lankan markets in the same period had highlighted attractive market valuations, it said.

Crosby said this year's sharp rises on Far Eastern markets, in line with those on major Western markets, had pushed up valuations, which might prompt some fund managers to divert funds to sub-continental markets.
